detail.body:
## Motivation

The Muse Spark Open recipes (and the DeepSeek-V3 recipes) enable two bundled kernel overrides by default: `fused_swiglu` and `helion_rope`. Both register their custom ops with `device_types="cuda"`, so on any other accelerator the first forward fails, even though the kernels themselves are Triton and Helion code that compiles fine for other backends:

```
NotImplementedError: The operator 'torchtitan::silu_and_mul' is not currently
implemented for the XPU device.
```

`helion_rope` also gated its fused path on `Tensor.is_cuda`. Off CUDA it silently fell back to the PyTorch complex RoPE, so the override reported as applied while doing nothing.

## Changes

1. **`fused_swiglu`**: register `torchtitan::silu_and_mul` and its backward for `torchtitan.tools.utils.device_type`, the detected accelerator. This is the same helper core torchtitan already uses for device selection, and it falls back to `"cuda"` when no accelerator is present.
2. **`helion_rope`**: same registration change. The `is_cuda` eligibility checks are replaced with `xq.device.type == device_type`, and the same-device check is kept.
3. **`fused_swiglu` kernel arguments**: `NUM_ROWS`, `NUM_OFFSETS` and every stride were `tl.constexpr`. `NUM_ROWS` is the routed-token count, which changes on every MoE layer and every step, so every launch with a new value compiled a new kernel. This affects CUDA too. These values only feed masks and address arithmetic, so they are now ordinary integer arguments. `NUM_COLS`, `HAS_OFFSETS` and the block sizes stay `constexpr`. Triton still specializes integer arguments on divisibility by 16 and on the value 1, so contiguous-stride codegen is unchanged.
4. **Tests**: `test_fused_swiglu.py`, `test_fused_swiglu_override.py` and `test_helion_rope.py` were gated on `torch.cuda.is_available()`, with skip reasons like "silu_and_mul op is CUDA-only". Gating, placement, `get_memory_info` and `synchronize` now go through `torch.accelerator`, so the tests run on non-CUDA backends instead of being skipped. CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Test plan

Unit tests with torch 2.16.0.dev20261008+xpu, triton-xpu 3.9.0, helion 1.5.1:

```
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/gpu/recipes/test_fused_swiglu.py \
    tests/unit_tests/gpu/recipes/test_fused_swiglu_override.py \
    tests/unit_tests/gpu/recipes/test_helion_rope.py
31 passed in 42.90s
```

These include `test_silu_and_mul_uses_int64_row_stride_arithmetic`, which covers strides past 2^31 now that they are runtime arguments, plus the Helion forward and backward numerics, `opcheck`, and the cross-device eligibility check.

On a CPU-only host the same command gives 15 passed and 16 skipped, with the accelerator tests skipping as before.

Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes all hooks. Pyrefly was run directly on the two override files and reports 0 errors.

<!-- ciflow-pending -->
The following ciflow label(s) have been added but CI has not been triggered yet because the workflows are awaiting approval:

- `ciflow/fake-pg`

Once a maintainer approves the workflows (scroll to the bottom of the PR page), the corresponding CI jobs will be triggered automatically. Please ping one of the reviewers if you do not have access to approve and run workflows.

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 1m 21s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/38986107160)

---
### Review: Run fused SwiGLU and Helion RoPE overrides on any accelerator

- [x] Gather the PR diff and context
- [x] Review `fused_swiglu.py` (op registration, constexpr changes)
- [x] Review `helion_rope.py` (registration, eligibility checks)
- [x] Review test changes
- [x] Post review

Overall this looks good. I didn't find any correctness bugs. The motivation is real: `device_types="cuda"` on Triton/Helion code was more restrictive than it needed to be, and the `is_cuda` gate in `helion_rope` silently fell back to the PyTorch path off CUDA while still reporting the override as applied. Most of what follows is about verification, plus a few small nits.

### Correctness checks (no action needed)

- **int64 address arithmetic still holds after dropping `constexpr`.** Now that strides are runtime args, Triton types any stride that fits in 32 bits as `i32`, so overflow was the main thing to rule out. `row_start = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK_M` (`fused_swiglu.py:64`, `:119`) makes `rows` int64, so `rows[:, None] * *_ROW_STRIDE` is promoted to int64 even when the stride is `i32`. The column terms use `i32` but are bounded by `NUM_COLS * col_stride`, which is small. `test_silu_and_mul_uses_int64_row_stride_arithmetic` (stride 8192, row offset past 2^31) covers exactly this case, so passing it on XPU is good evidence.
- **`row_limit` typing.** `row_limit = NUM_ROWS` followed by `row_limit = tl.load(...)` inside `if HAS_OFFSETS:` is fine because `HAS_OFFSETS` is still `constexpr`, so the branch is resolved at compile time.
- **The `_complex_eligible` rewrite** (`helion_rope.py:435`) is equivalent to the old four `is_cuda` checks. `xq.device.type == device_type` together with the chained `xq.device == xk.device == ...` implies that all four tensors are on the accelerator. On a CPU-only host `device_type` falls back to `"cuda"`, so CPU inputs are still ineligible and take the fallback as before.
- **Recompile fix.** Treating `NUM_ROWS` as `constexpr` really did force a recompile for every distinct routed-token count, on CUDA too. Making it and the strides runtime args is the right call. Specialization on `==1` and `%16` keeps the `COL_STRIDE == 1` fast path.

### Suggestions

1. **Show CUDA numerics and perf for the `constexpr` change.** This is the part of the PR that changes behaviour on the battle-tested CUDA path, and the test plan only covers XPU. Per CLAUDE.md ("Protect battle-tested code paths", "Show numerical proof"), please add:
   - A CUDA run of the three test files.
   - A short before/after microbenchmark of `silu_and_mul_forward_kernel` / `_backward_kernel` on CUDA at a representative MoE shape. Losing constant strides can change vectorization or index math. I expect any difference to be in the noise, and a real win once compile time is counted, but it's worth showing.
   - Ideally a 10-step DSv3 or Muse Spark debug run with `seed=42` / `deterministic=True` showing bit-identical loss and grad_norm on CUDA. The math is unchanged, so this should be trivially identical.

2. **Helion configs are tuned for GB200.** `_complex_fwd_config` / `_complex_bwd_config` (`helion_rope.py:220-274`) hard-code configs from a GB200 search: `num_warps=2`, `l2_groupings`, and `load_eviction_policies` of `first`/`last`. Off CUDA these compile, but they may perform worse than the PyTorch fallback. Please either add an XPU fused-vs-fallback timing to the PR description, or add a `# TODO` noting that these configs are CUDA-tuned. Otherwise, enabling the override by default on non-CUDA could end up a perf regression rather than a win.

3. **The tests and the op registration detect the device differently.** The ops register for `torchtitan.tools.utils.device_type`, which comes from `torch._utils._get_available_device_type()` and checks cuda/xpu/mtia/privateuse1 with a fallback to `"cuda"`. The tests gate on `torch.accelerator.is_available()` / `current_accelerator()`, which also covers backends such as MPS. On a host where the two disagree, for example an Apple Silicon dev box, the tests would now run and fail with `NotImplementedError` where they used to skip. A simple way to keep them consistent is to use the same source in the tests, e.g. `from torchtitan.tools.utils import device_type` and skip unless `torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()` has `.type == device_type`. Low priority, since CI has no MPS runners.
   [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20sg%2Fxpu-kernel-overrides%2C%20in%20tests%2Funit_tests%2Fgpu%2Frecipes%2Ftest_fused_swiglu.py%2C%20test_fused_swiglu_override.py%20and%20test_helion_rope.py%2C%20gate%20the%20accelerator%20tests%20on%20the%20same%20device%20type%20the%20custom%20ops%20register%20for%20(torchtitan.tools.utils.device_type)%20so%20that%20backends%20detected%20by%20torch.accelerator%20but%20not%20by%20_get_available_device_type%20(e.g.%20MPS)%20skip%20instead%20of%20failing.&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)

4. **Other overrides are still CUDA-only.** `fused_mla.py` (`:587`, `:604`, `:651`, `:719`, and the `x.is_cuda` check at `:995`) and `kimi_attention_residual.py` (`:540`, `:581`) still use `device_types="cuda"`. Keeping this PR scoped to the two overrides the recipes enable by default is fine. A sentence in the description saying the rest are intentionally left for later would help reviewers, given the "audit all callsites" guideline.

5. **Nit:** the warning text at `helion_rope.py:484`, "need accelerator q/k/cache/positions", could name the expected device to make debugging easier, e.g. `f"need {device_type} q/k/..."`.

### Summary

The core change is correct, and the int64-safety concern from moving strides to runtime args is handled by the existing `.to(tl.int64)` on `row_start`. The main gap is evidence on CUDA: no CUDA test, perf, or loss numbers are shown for the `constexpr` removal, and there is no XPU perf data showing that the GB200-tuned Helion configs beat the fallback. Items 3 to 5 are minor.

I didn't run the tests myself because this runner has no accelerator.
